Every Unix-like operating system uses a.why: Stated as a rule about the class in the newline article and in the many texts on CRLF versus LF. Rated unlikely rather than very_unlikely because it can also be generalised from members.

sources.quote: Unix followed the Multics practice, and later Unix-like systems followed Unix.
sources.note: Multics used LF alone; the newline table lists Unix and Unix-like systems (Linux, macOS, *BSD, ...) under LF.

Linux is a Unix-like operating system..why: Said in the first lines of the Linux article and very often elsewhere.
